provenance: I authored the Unique formalization and its additional evaluation checks, but did not author Shared or the correspondence implementation. For this cross-layer review I read all required authored units, exact Lean selections and the review-policy snapshot; I also inspected the named definitions and statement assumptions in any additionally listed source context. I compared the Shared design independently, found and requested correction of a stored-mode/path-mode wording mismatch, then reread the changed shared.steps snapshot and verified other required inputs unchanged before deciding. Listing a containing source context records the inspected definitions, not an audit of every proof tactic in that file.
rationale: unit:shared.embedding supplies E after the Given and Shared syntax/state dependencies introduce its source and target domains. embedId transfers the numeric index between distinct tagged ObjectId structures; embedReference adds unique mode to that embedded identity. embedSlots uses Option.map so None remains None and keys/list order stay fixed. embedObject preserves class and recursively embeds fields; embedState embeds all object keys and references while preserving variable names and the Nat counter. embedPlace recurses structurally; embedValue maps give and recursively maps all constructor argument expressions, with no giveShare branch. embedStatement, embedClasses, embedProgram and embedConfiguration preserve destinations, declarations, statement order and the pairing of code/storage. Thus 'identities preserved' means the same tagged numeric identity represented in the independent layer type, not Lean definitional equality across two different structures.
limitations: This comparison checks prose/notation and formal statement correspondence; it does not independently certify Lean proof checking or audit proof tactics.
